chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from a man, from Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He was asked about a man who broke his fast for one day in the month of Ramadan, so he said: 'Its expiation is two jaribs of food, and that is twenty sa'.'

key_terms.جَرِيبَانِ: Two jaribs (a unit of volume/area measure)
key_terms.صَاعاً: Sa' (a traditional unit of volume measure)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation (kaffarah) for breaking a fast in Ramadan for one day?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies the *kaffarah* (expiation) for intentionally breaking the fast in Ramadan as twenty *sa's* of food, a measure consistent with the baseline obligation in Surah Al-Baqarah. In Shia jurisprudence, this narration is often discussed alongside the *mud* (half *sa*) for unintentional breaks, highlighting the distinction between minor and major expiations based on the nature of the violation.
